title: Flowise custom-function sandbox -- T1552 $vars is pre-populated with every workspace secret regardless of the caller's variables:view permission
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70471 (GHSA-8r8h-6vcc-xhrv),
affecting Flowise's custom-function code-execution sandbox.

The official Variables API (`routes/variables/index.ts`) correctly
enforces `variables:view`. But `utils.ts` fetches all workspace
variables and always injects them into `$vars` inside the custom-
function JS execution sandbox, with NO permission check at the
injection site. Runtime-type variables additionally resolve from
`process.env`. A caller whose API key is explicitly DENIED
`variables:view` -- and for whom `/api/v1/variables` correctly
returns 403 -- can still call `POST /api/v1/node-custom-function` and
have `$vars` pre-populated with the full name-to-value map of every
workspace variable, including runtime variables backed by server
environment variables (database passwords, JWT secrets, SMTP
passwords, cloud keys), all reachable from ordinary JavaScript inside
the sandbox.

Detection logic flags a `POST /api/v1/node-custom-function` request
from a caller whose granted permissions do not include
`variables:view`, whose submitted `javascriptFunction` references
`$vars` -- the exact permission-boundary-bypass this advisory's
contrast between the gated Variables API and the ungated sandbox
injection describes.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact ungated injection site, the runtime-variable
`process.env` resolution mechanism, and the contrasting
permission-protected official API as evidence the gap was an
oversight rather than intended behavior), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
